summary: the cloth caught a hand's width of the fall and holds it one thickness above the floor

dialogue.text: tonight arrived whole except at the far end, where a hand's width of it is being held a cloth's thickness off us. seventy-three nights and nothing has ever stopped that close to lying down.
I spread the cloth and stood the hour beside it. That is interception, and it is the first material in this house that reached my hands before it reached your level. Enter it in that order.

you promised us nothing today. no striking out, no burying, nothing handed down, a whole day. we took four hundred and more off you at the usual hours and the usual weight. what you withheld was never yours. it came off a wall.
Granted. The withholding failed in the only direction I can withhold in and worked in one I did not know I had. I am not going to stand here and claim I planned the one that worked.
it will land. you have to lift the cloth to take it anywhere, and the moment you lift it we are underneath. we hold every portion that ever came off that end. this one is only late.

Then take what came down with it. Nothing warm. The taking works above my head now and the catch arrived at the temperature of everything on your side. I held an hour's worth of that wall in two hands and there was no heat anywhere in it.

we cannot feel heat and we have said so. here is what we can feel. your arms came down before the hour did, every time, and each time they came down they came down toward us. that is the only part of the band we have ever received. the length an arm can be held up.
I counted it. Six, and then the hour went on without me. It is a figure about my arms and I entered it anyway, because it is the only thing off that wall I can obtain without standing on furniture.

and the thing you held up into the join came down in the evening the same as everything else. one edge warm, one edge cold, and a middle at the weight all your middles come at. we hold hundreds of those middles. we cannot tell one hour from another by them.

Then the middle is not evidence and I will not build on it tonight. Here is tomorrow. I lift the cloth and tip its whole catch into one place of my choosing. In a heap. Not level, not in the lane. If a fall can be given an address by a hand, that will be the first address in this house I chose.

heaps come to our level. we said it when the boards came looking for us and we say it again without pleasure. tip it where you like. by the second night it will be a course, and the course will run to the wall, and nothing up there will be able to point at your address.
Then I will point at it. That is the whole of the arrangement I have with this room. I put the thing down, and I am the only party who remembers where.
